---
title: "Cities with Most Short-Haul Flights"
author: "Jeremy Handy"
date: "2026-10-21"
output: html_document
---
  
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(mapview)
library(leaflet)

# Use an explicit basemap instead of relying on defaults.
mapview::mapviewOptions(
  basemaps = "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas"
)

# Read the revised source data.
city_data <- read_csv(
  "data/Cities_with_most_short_flights_geo_data_2026.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Clean passenger totals and calculate ranks.
city_data <- city_data %>%
  mutate(
    Sum_of_Passengers = parse_number(
      as.character(Sum_of_Passengers)
    ),
    Rank = min_rank(desc(Sum_of_Passengers))
  ) %>%
  arrange(Rank)

# Check required fields.
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(city_data$Latitude)),
  all(!is.na(city_data$Longitude)),
  all(!is.na(city_data$Sum_of_Passengers))
)

# Convert market coordinates into spatial points.
Top_20_Candidates <- st_as_sf(
  city_data,
  coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)

# Read the 2016 U.S. primary roads shapefile.
roads <- st_read(
  "data/roads/tl_2016_us_primaryroads.shp",
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Transform roads into WGS 84 to match the city coordinates.
roads <- st_transform(roads, 4326)
```

```{r map, echo=FALSE}
# Render markets over the basemap.
market_map <- mapview(
  Top_20_Candidates,
  zcol = "Sum_of_Passengers",
  at = c(
    250000,
    500000,
    750000,
    1000000,
    1300000,
    1600000
  ),
  layer.name = "Short-Haul Passengers by Origin Market",
  popup = TRUE,
  legend = TRUE
)

# Add primary roads as a separate overlay.
roads_map <- mapview(
  roads,
  color = "#555555",
  lwd = 1,
  alpha.regions = 0,
  legend = FALSE,
  layer.name = "U.S. Primary Roads"
)

# Combine the two map layers.
market_map + roads_map
```
